title: Ionix pipeline run — 5 Aug 2026
heading: Full pipeline run
lede: A clean rebuild of every AUR package, a headless install driven entirely through QEMU screenshots, then a boot of the installed disk to see whether the desktop actually works — ending with a full web-to-wallpaper round trip. Every image below is a frame captured from the VM during that run.
notes:
Phase 1 produced no screenshots — it is a terminal build. clean.sh wiped localrepo/ including every .built-* sentinel, so all ~41 AUR packages compiled from source. docker-build.sh exited 0 with no FAILED_PACKAGES.

The only ERROR lines in the build log are pytest collection failures inside one package’s own test suite (a vcr API mismatch). That package still packaged cleanly.

Two findings, both in Phase 5. Downloading a wallpaper from Google Images and setting it through ctrl-super-w cannot be completed as intended: Google serves every image as .avif, and the picker’s only filter is *.jpg *.jpeg *.png *.gif with no All files option. Separately, ~/Pictures/Wallpapers — the folder the picker opens in — ships empty.

The wallpaper mechanism itself is fine. Given a supported file it works end to end, which the last three frames show.

phases.title: Headless install
phases.lede: Booted the ISO on a blank 64 GiB disk and drove Calamares by screenshot.

shots.title: Installer auto-launches
shots.note: The live session reaches Hyprland and ionix-first-login starts Calamares on its own — nothing to click to get here.

shots.title: Location, as shipped
shots.note: Defaults to America / New York.

shots.title: Region list
shots.note: Opening the region combo to pick Europe.

shots.title: Europe selected
shots.note: The zone falls back to Amsterdam and the number format follows it to Nederlands.

shots.title: Zone type-ahead
shots.note: Typing jumps the list straight to Copenhagen.

shots.title: Europe/Copenhagen set
shots.note: System language auto-follows to English (Denmark) — close, but not what we want.

shots.title: System locale dialog
shots.note: Currently en_DK.UTF-8.

shots.title: da_DK.UTF-8 selected
shots.note: Type-ahead again, this time in the locale list.

shots.title: Locale complete
shots.note: Both language and number format now read dansk (Danmark).

shots.title: Danish layout, already chosen
shots.note: The keyboard page inherits Danish from the locale. From here the guest remaps punctuation, so every value typed afterwards was kept alphanumeric.

shots.title: Partitioning
shots.note: One 64 GiB virtio disk, no existing table.

shots.title: Erase disk
shots.note: Resolves to a 512 MiB FAT32 ESP plus a 63.5 GiB ext4 root, no swap.

shots.title: Users page
shots.note: Empty, with strong passwords and shared root password both on.

shots.title: The auto-derive trap
shots.note: Typing the full name silently fills login lucasion and hostname lucasion-standardpc.

shots.title: Corrected
shots.note: Both fields cleared and retyped as ion and ionix.

shots.title: Password accepted
shots.note: Every field validates green and Next enables.

shots.title: Summary
shots.note: Timezone, Danish keyboard, and the full partition plan for /dev/vda.

shots.title: Point of no return
shots.note: prompt-install: true adds this extra confirmation before anything is written.

shots.title: Unpacking
shots.note: 8% in — and the progress text is already Danish, so the locale took effect during the install itself.

shots.title: All done
shots.note: About fourteen minutes from confirm to finish.

phases.title: The installed system
phases.lede: Rebooted from disk with no ISO attached.

shots.title: hyprlock on first boot
shots.note: Autologin lands on the lock screen, and it already knows the user: Welcome back, ion.

shots.title: Desktop
shots.note: Wallpaper and the Quickshell bar, started by its systemd user unit rather than exec-once.

shots.title: kitty, fish, oh-my-posh
shots.note: super-t. The prompt confirms user and hostname in one line.

shots.title: Proof of a real system
shots.note: Arch, kernel 7.1.5, 1274 packages, Hyprland 0.56.1 on Wayland, ext4 root, network up, and Locale: da_DK.UTF-8.

phases.title: Desktop under test
phases.lede: Exercising the parts most likely to regress.

shots.title: ionixtheme winix
shots.note: The bar relocates to a bottom, centred taskbar and the date format changes — hyprland, kitty, quickshell and ioexplorer all restyle live.

shots.title: ionixtheme ionix
shots.note: Round-trip back. The kitty config is restored from the backup the styler made on the way in.

shots.title: Audio popout
shots.note: Output / Input / Apps tabs, volume slider and device list. QEMU exposes only a dummy sink.

shots.title: Clock popout
shots.note: Calendar with Monday-first week ordering, matching the Danish locale, and today accented.

shots.title: Notification centre
shots.note: super-n, with the do-not-disturb toggle.

shots.title: The one non-result
shots.note: Clicking the green tray icon opened nothing. It reads as a real tray applet rather than a Quickshell module, so it is worth a look on hardware — but it is not a confirmed defect.

shots.title: Launcher
shots.note: alt-space. App names and descriptions render in Danish, so the locale reaches desktop entries too.

shots.title: ioexplorer
shots.note: Tiles beside kitty, and every XDG user directory exists.

shots.title: Workspace 2
shots.note: super-2. Empty, with the bar's active pill moved.

shots.title: Back to workspace 1
shots.note: Both windows exactly as they were left.

shots.title: Chrome first run
shots.note: super-w. The first-run page is Danish, and gnome-keyring asks to create a default keyring.

shots.title: Keyring dismissed
shots.note: Chrome settles into the tiling layout.

phases.title: Web to wallpaper
phases.lede: The longest path the desktop offers: browser to download to file chooser to background layer.

shots.title: Chrome, in Danish
shots.note: super-w. The keyring prompt and a restore-pages bubble both need dismissing first.

shots.title: Searching
shots.note: Typed straight into the omnibox — no punctuation, so the Danish layout cannot corrupt it. Google answers with a consent wall.

shots.title: Google Images
shots.note: Results load fine, confirming real network egress from the guest.

shots.title: Picking one
shots.note: A purple low-poly image, 740 × 555, in the preview panel.

shots.title: Save image as
shots.note: The Chrome context menu is Danish: Gem billede som…

shots.title: First finding
shots.note: The save dialog reveals the format: .avif. Google’s proxy re-encodes everything, whatever the source site hosts.

shots.title: Not a one-off
shots.note: A second, unrelated image saves as .avif too — and the first download is listed, 15.3 kB, sitting in ~/Downloads.

shots.title: Second finding
shots.note: ctrl-super-w opens the zenity picker at ~/Pictures/Wallpapers — which ships empty. Note the filter at bottom right.

shots.title: The file is invisible
shots.note: Same ~/Downloads the save dialog just listed a file in, and the picker shows nothing. The .avif is filtered out.

shots.title: No way around it
shots.note: The filter dropdown has exactly one entry and no All files escape hatch, so the downloaded image simply cannot be reached.

shots.title: A supported file
shots.note: grim writes a PNG to ~/Pictures. It appears immediately, with a thumbnail — so the picker is working, the format was the problem.

shots.title: Wallpaper set
shots.note: An empty workspace after OK. It looks like a terminal because the wallpaper is the screenshot — frozen at 17:03:59 while the live bar reads 17:07.

shots.title: Proof
shots.note: Every window closed — the terminal’s icon is gone from the bar — and the image is still there. Only the background layer can do that.
